Marry
MAR-ee
v.t. and v.i. (to enter the covenant union of husband and wife; rendering Hebrew laqach, ba'al, Greek gameo)
From Old French marier, Latin maritare, from maritus, a husband. Scripture's own vocabulary is plainer — Hebrew commonly says a man takes a wife, and the taking is a public, covenantal act with witnesses.

Biblical Definition

To marry is to enter the covenant union established at creation, which the Lord Jesus grounds not in Moses but in Genesis: God made them male and female, and “For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh” (Ephesians 5:31, citing Genesis 2:24). Three acts constitute it — leaving, cleaving, and becoming one flesh — in that order, so that a public separation from the parental household precedes the union rather than following it. Paul treats marriage as the ordinary and honourable estate while granting that singleness has real advantages for undivided service, and he is entirely unsentimental about the reason many should marry: “if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn” (1 Corinthians 7:9). He instructs the younger widows likewise: “I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, guide the house, give none occasion to the adversary to speak reproachfully” (1 Timothy 5:14). Hebrews states the estate's honour and its boundary in one verse: “Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge” (Hebrews 13:4). And the Lord Jesus sets its horizon: “in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven” (Matthew 22:30). Marriage is a creation ordinance for this age, pointing beyond itself to the union it pictures.

Webster 1828 Definition

To enter the creation covenant of one man and one woman. Christ grounds it in Genesis; Paul commends it plainly, including as a remedy for incontinence; Hebrews calls it honourable in all; and Christ says it does not continue in the resurrection.

expand to see more

MARRY, v.t. [Fr. marier; L. maritus, a husband.] To unite in wedlock or matrimony; to join a man and woman for life, and constitute them man and wife according to the laws or customs of a nation.

2. To dispose of in wedlock; as, a father marries his daughter.

3. To take for husband or wife.

MARRY, v.i. To enter into the conjugal state; to unite as husband and wife.

5. It is better to marry than to burn. 1 Cor. 7.

Key Scripture

Ephesians 5:31 — "For this cause shall a man leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh."

1 Corinthians 7:9 — "But if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn."

Hebrews 13:4 — "Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge."

Matthew 22:30 — "For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven."

Modern Corruption

Marriage has been redefined from a covenant instituted by God between one man and one woman into a contract of mutual satisfaction terminable at will, and then extended to unions Scripture does not recognise — while a rival error inside the church denigrates it as second-best to celibacy.

expand to see more

Two redefinitions have proceeded together, and the first made the second possible. Once marriage was recast as a private arrangement for the happiness of the parties, its permanence became negotiable, its exclusivity optional, and the sexes of the parties incidental — because a contract of mutual satisfaction has no principle limiting it. Scripture's account is different at the root: marriage is a creation ordinance, established before the fall, instituted by God rather than by the couple or the state, with a Witness present at every wedding, and it is the appointed picture of Christ and the church (Ephesians 5:32). That is why the sexes are not incidental — the picture requires a husband and a bride — and why permanence is not a preference. The dictionary holds the one-man-one-woman-for-life standard as the Lord Jesus stated it in Matthew 19, with the single exception He named, and holds it with pastoral care for the many whose marriages have failed, since a standard restated is not a stone thrown.

The opposite corruption is older and arose inside the church: the elevation of celibacy into a higher spiritual state, with marriage tolerated as a concession to weakness. It produced enforced clerical celibacy, monastic vows, and the reading of 1 Corinthians 7 as though Paul preferred virginity in principle. Paul says something narrower — that in a present distress the unmarried are freer for undivided service — and he says elsewhere that forbidding to marry is a doctrine of devils (1 Timothy 4:1-3). Hebrews 13:4 settles it: marriage is honourable in all. The Reformers married deliberately and publicly for this reason, and the pastor's household became one of Protestantism's most visible arguments.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew laqach (to take, as a man takes a wife) and ba'al (to be master of, to marry); Greek gameo (to marry) and gamizo (to give in marriage), with gamos, the wedding itself.

expand to see more

Hebrew laqach (H3947) — to take, receive; the ordinary idiom for taking a wife throughout the Old Testament.

Hebrew dabaq (H1692) — to cleave, cling; the verb of Genesis 2:24 rendered joined unto in Ephesians 5:31.

Greek gameo (G1060) — to marry; the verb in 1 Corinthians 7:9 and Matthew 22:30.

Greek gamos (G1062) — a wedding, marriage feast; the word in Hebrews 13:4 and in the parables of the marriage supper.

Greek mysterion (G3466) — a mystery, a truth once hidden now revealed; Paul's term for what marriage pictures in Ephesians 5:32.

Usage

"“Leave… be joined… one flesh” — three acts in a fixed order; the public leaving precedes the union."

"“Better to marry than to burn” — Paul's entirely unsentimental counsel."

"“In the resurrection they neither marry” — a creation ordinance for this age, pointing past itself."
